OPSC Petrologist 2021 Paper-II • Q001

📐 Law of Superposition & Stratigraphic Principles

Discipline: Sedimentology & Stratigraphy Paper Code: GPGM - 3/20 Source: OPSC Petrologist Examination
Official Examination Question
An undeformed sedimentary layer is _______ than the layer above and ______ than the layer below.
(A) Younger — Younger
(B) Younger— Older
(C) Older— Younger
(D) Older—Older
Part I

Theoretical Principles & Core Geology Foundations

1. Fundamental Geological Principles & Core Concepts

This question examines Law of Superposition & Stratigraphic Principles in the discipline of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy.

In standard geological investigations, the established governing principles demonstrate that: Older—Younger (Law of Superposition: in an undeformed sequence, older strata lie below and younger strata lie above).

Standard Reference Axiom:

Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 16, pp. 501-505); G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, p. 280)

Part II

Forensic Option Dissection & Error Analysis

Option (A): Younger — Younger — INCORRECT

Does not satisfy the primary diagnostic criteria for this geological phenomenon.

Option (B): Younger— Older — INCORRECT

Represents an alternative or contrasting geological classification.

Option (C): Older— Younger — CORRECT ANSWER

Accurately satisfies the foundational geological definition and authoritative exam criteria.

Option (D): Older—Older — INCORRECT

Fails to meet the specific requirements of the question statement.

Part III

Synthesis Matrix & High-Yield Practice Problems

Summary & Diagnostic Matrix

Parameter Exam Specification Standard Reference Grounding
Topic & Discipline Law of Superposition & Stratigraphic Principles Sedimentology & Stratigraphy
Verified Correct Answer Option (C): Older— Younger Older—Younger (Law of Superposition: in an undeformed sequence, older strata lie below and younger strata lie above)
Authoritative Source Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 16, pp. 501-505); G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, p. 280)

High-Yield Practice Questions

Practice Q1: Which primary diagnostic criterion distinguishes this phenomenon in field investigations?
Answer: Verified Option (C) (Older— Younger)
Explanation: Grounded in standard geological principles as outlined in Sam Boggs Jr. (Principles of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy, Ch. 16, pp. 501-505).
Practice Q2: In comparative exam scenarios, how is this parameter typically evaluated?
Answer: Consistent with Law of Superposition & Stratigraphic Principles guidelines.
Explanation: Systematic petrological and stratigraphic frameworks confirm Option (C) as the definitive benchmark.

⏳ Radiometric Geochronology & Absolute Time

Discipline: Sedimentology & Stratigraphy Paper Code: GPGM - 3/20 Source: OPSC Petrologist Examination
Official Examination Question
Radiometric age is often referred to as ___age.
(A) Total
(B) Absolute
(C) Historic
(D) Geologic
Part I

Theoretical Principles & Core Geology Foundations

1. Fundamental Geological Principles & Core Concepts

This question examines Radiometric Geochronology & Absolute Time in the discipline of Sedimentology & Stratigraphy.

In standard geological investigations, the established governing principles demonstrate that: Absolute (Radiometric dating yields numerical/absolute ages in mega-annum Ma or giga-annum Ga).

Standard Reference Axiom:

G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, pp. 282-285); Faure & Mensing (Isotopes: Principles & Applications)

Part II

Forensic Option Dissection & Error Analysis

Option (A): Total — INCORRECT

Does not satisfy the primary diagnostic criteria for this geological phenomenon.

Option (B): Absolute — CORRECT ANSWER

Accurately satisfies the foundational geological definition and authoritative exam criteria.

Option (C): Historic — INCORRECT

Not the appropriate classification under the established stratigraphic and petrological guidelines.

Option (D): Geologic — INCORRECT

Fails to meet the specific requirements of the question statement.

Part III

Synthesis Matrix & High-Yield Practice Problems

Summary & Diagnostic Matrix

Parameter Exam Specification Standard Reference Grounding
Topic & Discipline Radiometric Geochronology & Absolute Time Sedimentology & Stratigraphy
Verified Correct Answer Option (B): Absolute Absolute (Radiometric dating yields numerical/absolute ages in mega-annum Ma or giga-annum Ga)
Authoritative Source G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, pp. 282-285); Faure & Mensing (Isotopes: Principles & Applications)

High-Yield Practice Questions

Practice Q1: Which primary diagnostic criterion distinguishes this phenomenon in field investigations?
Answer: Verified Option (B) (Absolute)
Explanation: Grounded in standard geological principles as outlined in G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, pp. 282-285).
Practice Q2: In comparative exam scenarios, how is this parameter typically evaluated?
Answer: Consistent with Radiometric Geochronology & Absolute Time guidelines.
Explanation: Systematic petrological and stratigraphic frameworks confirm Option (B) as the definitive benchmark.

☢️ U-Pb Radioactive Decay Series (U-238 to Pb-206)

Discipline: Mineralogy & Geochemistry Paper Code: GPGM - 3/20 Source: OPSC Petrologist Examination
Official Examination Question
Uranium-238 decays to which of the following daughter isotopes ?
(A) Rubidium — 87
(B) Uranium —235
(C) Lead —206
(D) Nitrogen-14
Part I

Theoretical Principles & Core Geology Foundations

1. Fundamental Geological Principles & Core Concepts

This question examines U-Pb Radioactive Decay Series (U-238 to Pb-206) in the discipline of Mineralogy & Geochemistry.

In standard geological investigations, the established governing principles demonstrate that: Lead-206 (238U decays via alpha and beta cascades to stable 206Pb with t_1/2 = 4.47 Ga).

Standard Reference Axiom:

G.B. Mahapatra (Text Book of Geology, p. 284); Dickin (Radiogenic Isotope Geology, Ch. 5)

Part II

Forensic Option Dissection & Error Analysis

Option (A): Rubidium — 87 — INCORRECT

Does not satisfy the primary diagnostic criteria for this geological phenomenon.

Option (B): Uranium —235 — INCORRECT

Represents an alternative or contrasting geological classification.

Option (C): Lead —206 — CORRECT ANSWER

1. Fundamental Geological Principles & Core Concepts

(D) Sonorous
Part I

Theoretical Principles & Core Geology Foundations

1. Fundamental Geological Principles & Core Concepts

This question examines Shear Zone Rheology & Ductile Shear Displacement in the discipline of Structural Geology & Tectonics.

In standard geological investigations, the established governing principles demonstrate that: Ductile (Shear zones are tabular zones of localized continuous ductile shear strain without loss of material continuity).

Standard Reference Axiom:

Haakon Fossen (Structural Geology, Ch. 15, pp. 340-365); Ramsay & Huber

Part II

Forensic Option Dissection & Error Analysis

Option (A): Ductile — CORRECT ANSWER

Accurately satisfies the foundational geological definition and authoritative exam criteria.

Option (B): Brittle — INCORRECT

Represents an alternative or contrasting geological classification.

Option (C): Malleable — INCORRECT

Not the appropriate classification under the established stratigraphic and petrological guidelines.

Option (D): Sonorous — INCORRECT

Fails to meet the specific requirements of the question statement.

Represents an alternative or contrasting geological classification.

Option (C): The layers on the upper side of the drag fold slides away from synclincal axis — INCORRECT

Not the appropriate classification under the established stratigraphic and petrological guidelines.

Option (D): The axes of the drag folds are not parallel to those of the major folds ' — CORRECT ANSWER

Accurately satisfies the foundational geological definition and authoritative exam criteria.
